# Fixture provenance

| File | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| `hpke-xwing-vector.json` | One entry (KEM `0x647a` MLKEM768-X25519, KDF `0x0001`, AEAD `0x0003`) copied unchanged from `src/crypto/hpke/testdata/hpke-pq.json` in Go 1.26.0. Go's licence (BSD-3-Clause) is in `LICENSE-go.txt`. It pins the X-Wing KEM of `draft-ietf-hpke-pq`. |
| `pedersen-h.json`, `kdf.json`, `disclosure-key-fingerprint.json`, `envelope.json`, `keyring.json`, `cbor.json`, `sign.json`, `secret-normalization.json` | Generated by `make fixtures` from this repository's code. The Argon2id answers were first checked against Node 24's `crypto.argon2Sync`, and the ristretto255 values against `@noble/curves`. The fingerprint answers were also computed by hand with Python's `hashlib`. The envelope and the keyring copies are opened by `scripts/check-fixtures.mjs` with Node's own crypto (HKDF, AES-256-GCM and, on Node 24, Argon2id), which `make test` runs; Node's Ed25519 checks every signature of `sign.json`; the normalization answers were made by Go's `x/text` and are checked by Node's own `normalize` and, on Node 24, Argon2id; and `github.com/fxamacker/cbor` (a test-only dependency) agrees with every value of `cbor.json` and with 3,000 random values. |
| `hpke-xwing-aes256gcm-sample.json` | Generated once by `make fixtures` (a seal is random, so it is not regenerated). Opened by Go, Node and the Go SDK. |
| `pedersen.json` | Generated by `make fixtures` from a fixed random source. `scripts/check-fixtures-noble.mjs` checks it with `@noble/curves` (`H`, every share against its commitments, the commitments hash, every group that rebuilds the secret, the refused shares, the resharing and the refused contribution). Noble shares no code with the Go library. |
| `holder-wrap.json` | Generated by `make fixtures` (the salt and nonce are fixed). Node's own HKDF and AES-256-GCM open both wraps in `scripts/check-fixtures.mjs`; the contact's Argon2id comes from Node 24's `crypto.argon2Sync`, or from `@noble/hashes` on older Node. |
| `share-envelope.json` | Generated once by `make fixtures` (a seal is random, so it is not regenerated). Its `release` part was rebuilt once for release format 2 (the signed share envelope inside the release); `make fixtures` does that for a fixture in the old format and leaves the dealing and the envelope as they were. Go opens the envelope and the release and refuses every change (`holder/fixture_test.go`). `scripts/check-fixtures-noble.mjs` checks, with `@noble/curves`, everything that needs no HPKE: the Ed25519 signatures, the statement bytes (deterministic CBOR), the share against the commitments and the inner key salt; on Node 24 it also checks the Argon2id key of the release. |
| `webhook-signature.json` | Known answers for the `Custodian-Signature` webhook header. The first signature was produced by custodian-api's `webhook.Sign`; the others follow the same rule. Both SDKs must accept and refuse exactly these. |
| `MANIFEST.json` | SHA-256 of every other file here. SDKs that vendor these files fail their tests if a hash differs. |
